papers.title: Bariatric Orthopaedics: Total Hip Arthroplasty in Super-Obese Patients (Those with a BMI of ≥50 kg/m2)
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The purpose of this study was to assess the clinical and patient-reported outcomes of primary total hip arthroplasty in super-obese patients (those with a body mass index [BMI] of ≥50 kg/m(2)) compared with a matched group of patients who had a normal BMI (<30 kg/m(2)). A secondary objective was to assess patients' experiences in finding a treating surgeon. METHODS: Forty-eight hips in forty-five patients who had a minimum BMI of 50 kg/m(2) and who had undergone a primary total hip arthroplasty at one of four high-volume institutions between 2001 and 2010 were reviewed. This included twenty-six women and nineteen men who had a mean age of fifty-four years (range, thirty-six to seventy-one years) and who were followed for a mean time of six years (range, four to twelve years). These patients were compared in a 1:3 ratio with a non-obese matched group (those with a BMI of <30 kg/m(2)) of 135 patients who had undergone total hip arthroplasty during the same time period by the same surgeons. The outcomes evaluated included implant survivorship, complication rates, Harris hip scores, 36-item Short-Form (SF)-36 questionnaires, University of California Los Angeles (UCLA) activity scores, and patient experience in finding a treating surgeon. RESULTS: The super-obese group had a 4.5 times higher odds ratio of undergoing a revision when compared with the matching group (p = 0.06); the overall implant survivorship was 89.6% for the super-obese group and 97.8% for the matching group. The super-obese group also had a significantly higher odds ratio (7.7) of complications compared with the matching group (p = 0.017). The super-obese group also had significantly lower mean values for the Harris hip score (82 points for the super-obese group compared with 91 points for the matched group; p = 0.002), the SF-36 Physical Component Summary score (39 points for the super-obese group and 49 points for the matched group; p = 0.001), the SF-36 Mental Component Summary scores (46 points for the super-obese group and 58 points for the matched group; p = 0.001), and the UCLA activity score (3.9 points for the super-obese group compared with 6.2 points for the matched group; p = 0.001). Compared with the matched group, super-obese patients were evaluated by a larger number of orthopaedic surgeons prior to undergoing total hip arthroplasty. CONCLUSIONS: The clinical and patient-reported outcomes of primary total hip arthroplasty were lower in the super-obese patients. These patients also faced challenges in finding surgeons who would perform their procedure. Super-obese patients may benefit from counseling with their treating surgeon to set realistic expectations with regard to the outcomes of their procedure.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文仅关注超肥胖患者全髋关节置换的临床结果，未涉及任何生物力学建模或应力分析。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a purely clinical outcomes study with no biomechanical modeling, no FE analysis, no stress shielding quantification, no micromotion assessment, and no comparison of intact vs implanted femur.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较超肥胖与正常BMI患者全髋关节置换的临床结局
summary_zh.method: 回顾性队列研究，匹配比例1:3
summary_zh.result: 超肥胖组翻修率和并发症更高，功能评分更低
summary_zh.validation: 临床随访数据统计分析

summary_en.motivation: To compare clinical and patient-reported outcomes of primary total hip arthroplasty in super-obese patients versus a matched normal-BMI cohort.
summary_en.method: Retrospective matched cohort study (1:3 ratio) of 48 hips in super-obese patients and 135 controls from four high-volume institutions.
summary_en.result: Super-obese patients had higher revision rates (OR 4.5), more complications (OR 7.7), and significantly worse Harris hip scores and SF-36 scores.
summary_en.validation: Clinical follow-up with statistical comparison of implant survivorship and patient-reported outcomes.

papers.title: Structural investigation of selective laser melting and electron beam melting of Ti-6Al-4V using neutron diffraction
papers.first_author_affiliation: Material Science Department, Nuclear Research Center-Negev, Beer-Sheva, Israel

corresponding_authors.name: Eitan Tiferet
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Material Science Department, Nuclear Research Center-Negev, Beer-Sheva, Israel

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文研究了选区激光熔化和电子束熔化Ti-6Al-4V的结构特性，但未涉及多孔结构、应力遮挡或疲劳性能等生物医学植入体核心问题。
llm.why_not_core: No porous structure design, no mechanical testing (static or fatigue), no stress shielding evaluation, and no osseointegration or surface characterization relevant to biomedical implants.

summary_zh.motivation: 了解增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的微观结构和残余应力
summary_zh.method: 利用中子衍射表征SLM和EBM样品的晶体结构和应力
summary_zh.result: 揭示了不同工艺下的织构和残余应力分布差异

summary_en.motivation: To characterize the crystallographic texture and residual stress in additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V via neutron diffraction.
summary_en.method: Selective laser melting (SLM) and electron beam melting (EBM) samples were analyzed using neutron diffraction to determine phase composition, texture, and residual stress.
summary_en.result: Differences in texture and residual stress were observed between SLM and EBM, attributed to distinct thermal histories.
